content: Amoxicillin-clavulanate potassium, commonly known as AUGMENTIN, can be taken with or without food. However, the absorption of clavulanate potassium is improved when the medication is administered at the start of a meal. To reduce the likelihood of gastrointestinal side effects, it is recommended to take AUGMENTIN at the beginning of a meal. Adults The standard adult dosage is one 500-mg tablet of AUGMENTIN every 12 hours or one 250-mg tablet every 8 hours. For more severe infections, including respiratory tract infections, the recommended dosage is one 875-mg tablet every 12 hours or one 500-mg tablet every 8 hours. Adults who have difficulty swallowing tablets may use the 125 mg/5 mL or 250 mg/5 mL oral suspension as a substitute for the 500-mg tablet. Similarly, the 200 mg/5 mL or 400 mg/5 mL suspension can be used in place of the 875-mg tablet. It is important to note that two 250-mg tablets should not be substituted for one 500-mg tablet, as both contain the same amount of clavulanic acid (125 mg as the potassium salt). Therefore, two 250-mg tablets are not equivalent to one 500-mg tablet. Additionally, the 250-mg tablet and the 250-mg chewable tablet are not interchangeable because they contain different amounts of clavulanic acid. Pediatric Patients For neonates and infants under 12 weeks (3 months) of age, the recommended dosage of AUGMENTIN is 30 mg/kg/day, divided every 12 hours, based on the amoxicillin component. Due to limited experience with the 200 mg/5 mL formulation in this age group, the 125 mg/5 mL oral suspension is recommended. For pediatric patients aged 12 weeks (3 months) and older, dosing regimens should follow the provided guidelines. The every-12-hour regimen is preferred as it is associated with significantly less diarrhea. However, the every-12-hour suspension (200 mg/5 mL and 400 mg/5 mL) and chewable tablets (200 mg and 400 mg) contain aspartame and should not be used by patients with phenylketonuria (PKU). Pediatric patients weighing 40 kg or more should follow adult dosing recommendations. Patients with Renal Impairment In general, patients with impaired renal function do not require a dose adjustment unless the impairment is severe. Patients with a glomerular filtration rate (GFR) of less than 30 mL/min should not receive the 875-mg dose. For those with a GFR of 10 to 30 mL/min, the recommended dose is 500 mg or 250 mg every 12 hours, depending on the severity of the infection. For patients with a GFR of less than 10 mL/min, the recommended dose is 500 mg or 250 mg every 24 hours, depending on the severity of the infection. Patients undergoing hemodialysis should receive 500 mg or 250 mg every 24 hours, depending on the severity of the infection. An additional dose should be administered both during and at the end of dialysis. Directions for Mixing Oral Suspension To prepare the oral suspension at the time of dispensing: 1. Tap the bottle until all the powder flows freely. 2. Add approximately two-thirds of the total amount of water required for reconstitution and shake vigorously to suspend the powder. 3. Add the remaining water and shake vigorously again. Note: Shake the oral suspension well before each use. The reconstituted suspension must be stored under refrigeration and discarded after 10 days.
